profile.headline: Aspiring Developer
profile.summary:
I graduated from Boise State University with a bachelor's degree in Games, Interactive Media, and Mobile Technology-- GIMM for short. During my education, I've pursued a variety of skills that align with my interests such as graphic design, coding languages, storytelling, writing, and programming. Alongside more serious studies, I also used the opportunity to try new things like learning mythology, education standards, and fencing!

In my free time, I enjoy creating concepts and working on all sorts of creative projects. I greatly enjoy programming new things, creating artwork, and creative writing. I hope that both present and future opportunities continue to allow me to combine all of these skills and hobbies into something worthwhile.

positions.title: Web Developer
positions.description: Maintain and facilitate updates and additions to CapEd owned websites. Troubleshoot and fix any issues related to features and contents available on those websites. Create and plan complete overhauls of older websites and website systems including migrations of content to new CMS platforms. May assist in other development related projects within the company. Use a variety of languages and frameworks including JavaScript, Bootstrap, Express, EJS, mySQL, and PHP.

positions.title: Fuel Station Attendant
positions.description: Provided exceptional customer service interactions resulting in an increase in both positive customer reviews and repeat customers for the business. Collaborated with management, coworkers, and corporate to raise workplace productivity and efficiency. Created improved versions of day-to-day documentation and signage and assisted in scheduling.

positions.title: Student Instructor
positions.description: Collaborated with a student-led group to engage in introduction level lectures about the Swift programming language to a variety of high school classrooms. Researched, compiled, and created lesson plans and schedules to ensure all information was informative, accurate, and applied to its fullest extent and within the lecture’s allotted time. Aided students and reiterated complex concepts to ensure all materials were being understood rather than copied.

positions.title: Programming and Graphical Intern
positions.description: Formulated, executed, tested, and iterated UI designs, graphics, and website features using the Django and Babylon.js frameworks. Created 3D renders built for web interactions in a workflow that utilized both SketchUp and Maya. Managed employee timesheets and payroll information to maintain validity and accuracy.

positions.title: Peer Mentor
positions.description: Mentored college freshmen by providing assistance, advice, and leadership to create a successful academic year. Managed the responsibilities and schedule of a small student group that worked on engineering a community service project to benefit the homeless.

projects.title: Idaho CapEd Foundation Website
projects.description: This project tasked me with overhauling the Idaho CapEd Foundation website with many improvements made along the way. From planning/creating a new database structure for processing inputted user data and reporting to implementing more robust spam prevention, I worked to create a site that was easier to use and maintain for all levels of users while also implementing a clean graphic and layout overhaul for the front-end aspects of the website. The website handles anything from application submissions, data reporting, user voting, and sending notifications for every milestone reached.

projects.title: Old Idaho Penitentiary AR App
projects.description: An Augmented Reality app programmed in Unity for use by the Idaho Historical Society. The app contains a map of image targets that users are able to scan in order to watch documentary-style information videos directly about the location they're standing at. All of the videos are scripted, edited, and created by our student development team and is slated to go live on location in May 2019!
